work_order.understanding: Two report spreadsheets narrow their category axis in JS with a plain substring test, `name.toLowerCase().includes(value.toLowerCase())`, while the query they sit on top of compiles `contains` to `$like '%' + value + '%'` and the AQL compiler emits that as `UNICODE_LIKE(<normalised pattern>, NORMALISE(name))` (aql/compiler.ts:735). UNICODE_LIKE speaks a PATTERN language, not a substring language: `%` and `?` are wildcards, a backslash escapes exactly those two, and both sides are diacritic-folded. budgetDataQuery.ts:246-265 already routes `contains` / `doesNotContain` through `likePatternToRegex(getNormalisedString('%' + value + '%')).test(getNormalisedString(textValue))` and the Custom and Grouped reports inherit that. The two sites named by the ticket never got the fix, so they disagree with Custom/Grouped about what a filter value means. I ran both code paths side by side over the fixture names Food, Groceries, 100% Off, Café, C_Sharp and 5 of 16 operator/value pairs diverge — including three the ticket does not even mention: `?`, `\\%`, and the diacritic case `cafe` (which today drops `Café`). The ordinary-substring case agrees, which is why this survives in the shipped product.
work_order.root_cause:
sankey-spreadsheet.ts:459-470 (`matchesStringCondition`, reached from `filterCategoryGroups`) and budget-analysis-spreadsheet.ts:246-255 (the `contains` / `doesNotContain` arms of the per-condition filter inside `createBudgetAnalysisSpreadsheet`) each reimplement the LIKE-pattern translation as a substring test. The pattern language the query actually speaks is defined once, in loot-core/src/shared/likePattern.ts, and the desktop client already has the reference implementation of the correct routing in budgetDataQuery.ts — the two sites just never call it.

One correction to the ticket's description, which matters because the implementer must not invent a screen that does not exist: Budget Analysis is **not** a per-category grid. `BudgetAnalysis.tsx` renders `BudgetAnalysisGraph` over `BudgetAnalysisData.intervalData`, which is one point per MONTH (budgeted / spent / balance / overspendingAdjustment). There are no per-category rows or cells. What the ticket calls "the filtered list decides which categories get a cell in the grid" is, in this code, that `categoriesToInclude` is the exact set every month's totals are summed over by `summarizeMonthCategories` (budget-analysis-spreadsheet.ts:88-151, called at :314 and :339). So the money risk the ticket names is real and correctly identified — an excluded category contributes nothing to `totalBudgeted` / `totalSpent` / `intervalData[].balance`, silently and with no error — but it arrives through the totals, not through a missing row. AC-4 and AC-5 below are written against what the code does; QA must not go looking for grid cells.
work_order.approach: Route both sites' `contains` and `doesNotContain` arms through the two primitives the query itself uses, `likePatternToRegex` and `getNormalisedString` from `@actual-app/core/shared`, copying budgetDataQuery.ts:246-265 including the comments that explain why `matches` is deliberately excluded and why the `$notlike` `OR IS NULL` disjunct never fires for a category name. Two changes, both local, no new shared module: (1) in sankey-spreadsheet.ts add a file-local `containsLikePattern(textValue, pattern)` helper and rewrite the two arms of `matchesStringCondition` to call it — no other function in that file changes; (2) in budget-analysis-spreadsheet.ts lift the existing `relevantConditions` → `categoriesToInclude` block out of the `createBudgetAnalysisSpreadsheet` closure verbatim into a new exported pure `filterCategoriesForConditions(baseCategories, categoryGroups, conditions, conditionsOp)`, rewrite its two text arms to call the same local helper, and have the closure call the new function in one line. The extraction exists only because AC-6 requires unit-level differential cases in budget-analysis-spreadsheet.test.ts and that logic is currently unreachable from outside an async closure that talks to the server; `isBaseCategory`, `summarizeMonthCategories` and `getNextRunningBalance` were extracted from that same closure for the same reason, so it is the file's established shape. `matches`, the query side, `UNICODE_LIKE` and rule evaluation are untouched.

files.why: The ticket's Sankey surface. `matchesStringCondition` is already called with the right text for both fields — `cat.name` for a category condition, `group.name` for a category_group condition (via `categoryMatchesConditions` at :487-511) — so fixing the two text arms fixes both fields at once.

The ticket's Budget Analysis surface, plus the extraction AC-6 depends on. The logic under repair is currently only reachable from inside an async closure that calls `send(...)`, so no unit test can reach it; the three helpers the existing test file already imports from this module were extracted for the same reason.

risks: OVER-NARROWING MOVES MONEY. This is the ticket's own stated risk and it is the one to guard. On Budget Analysis the filtered list IS the summand set for every total (:314, :339), so an axis stricter than the month data silently deletes a category's budgeted and spent amounts from the report with no error and no empty state; on Sankey it deletes a node's value. The fix must be at least as permissive as the query, never stricter. The `\\%` and `cafe` cases are what catch an over-escaping fix, and the `oo` / `BILL` negative controls are what catch an over-broad one.

A BEHAVIOUR CHANGE THE TICKET DID NOT NAME: diacritic folding. Today a filter of `contains "cafe"` drops a category named `Café` from both reports; after this change it is kept, because `getNormalisedString` folds the accent exactly as `NORMALISE` does on the query side. This is correct — it is what Custom and Grouped have done since budgetDataQuery.ts landed — but it will change rows for anyone filtering on accented category names. It is asserted in tests[] so it cannot drift back silently.

`filterCategoryGroups` applies conditions whose `customName` is set; `filterCategoriesByConditions` excludes them (its `!cond.customName` guard). That divergence is pre-existing and this change does not touch it, but it means the differential tests must use conditions with a falsy `customName` — the existing Sankey tests already use `customName: ''`, which is falsy and therefore compatible.

alternatives_considered.approach: Escape the user's wildcards at the axis site — treat `contains` as a literal substring match by regex-escaping `value` before the `includes`, so `%` matches only a literal percent sign.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It inverts the bound direction the ticket names. The query sends `%` to UNICODE_LIKE as a wildcard, so escaping at the axis makes the axis STRICTER than the set that was fetched — on Budget Analysis that deletes a category's budgeted and spent amounts from every total, which is the money-moving case the ticket singles out. It would also leave the two reports disagreeing with Custom and Grouped, which is the ticket's actual subject.

alternatives_considered.approach: Stop narrowing the axis at these two sites entirely — drop the JS filter from `filterCategoryGroups` and from the Budget Analysis closure and let both reports show every category, the way the unfiltered report does.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It fixes the loss by making the filter a no-op, which is a worse lie: the user asks for a filter and the report answers a different question with no indication. AC-7 explicitly requires ordinary substrings to keep narrowing, and the negative controls in tests[] would fail.

alternatives_considered.approach: Change `likePatternToRegex` or `UNICODE_LIKE` so a bare `%` is treated as a literal.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It changes the contract every report and the rules engine already agree on, to fix two call sites that had not conformed to it. The ticket puts this out of scope, and budgetDataQuery.ts:246-265 already documents the correct direction.

alternatives_considered.approach: Extract one shared `categoryMatchesTextCondition` into budgetDataQuery.ts and route all three sites through it, so the LIKE-pattern translation lives in exactly one place.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would make budgetDataQuery.ts define the contract, which is the opposite of what this slice is for ('this slice conforms to it, it does not define it'), and would rewrite already-correct, already-tested code inside that file. The duplicated helper is four lines, each copy carries a comment naming budgetDataQuery.ts as its reference, and budgetDataQuery.ts's own `evaluateCondition` closure stays untouched. Noted in out_of_scope in case a human wants the consolidation as its own ticket.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix only `contains`, leaving `doesNotContain` as the current negated substring test.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would make the two operators disagree with each other rather than with the query: `doesNotContain '%'` would then exclude every category the query fetched. The ticket's AC-2 requires them to be exact complements at the same value, which only holds if both read the pattern the same way.

assumptions: `api/budget-month` (Sankey) and `envelope-budget-month` (Budget Analysis) are still fetched with no conditions, as sankey-spreadsheet.ts:425-428 and budget-analysis-spreadsheet.ts:331 state. If a later change starts passing conditions down, both filters in this plan become dead weight rather than wrong — but that is a later change's ticket, not this one.

`allCategoryGroups` from `send('get-categories')` is structurally assignable to `Array<{ id: string; name: string }>`. If the implementer hits a type error, widen the parameter to `CategoryGroupEntity[]` — either compiles, and neither changes behaviour.

The report filter UI accepts a bare `%` or `?` in the value field without escaping it. It is a plain text input feeding `RuleConditionEntity.value` verbatim, and the existing code already stores raw values, so this holds.

`filterCategoriesByConditions` is a sound reference to hold the two sites to: it is the implementation Custom and Grouped reports actually ship, it is already covered by budgetDataQuery.test.ts, and it is the code the ticket cites as the contract.
unknowns: Whether any existing Sankey or Budget Analysis widget in the wild has a saved `conditions` payload with a category `contains` value containing `%`, `?` or a backslash. Such a widget's node set and totals will change on upgrade. Nothing in the repo can answer this, and no migration is warranted — the old behaviour was the bug — but it is the one thing a person might want to know before shipping.

Whether the Sankey report's zero-value `.filter` at :351 ever interacts badly with a `%` filter in a way QA will see as a regression. It should not (a zero-budgeted category had no node before either), but AC-1 states the non-zero qualifier explicitly so QA does not read it as a miss.
work_order.confidence_rationale: The defect is reproduced rather than inferred, the reference implementation and its tests exist in the same directory and are quoted in the ticket, and the two sites are the only two matches for the buggy expression across the whole reports tree. The 13-point haircut is for three things I could not execute: node_modules is absent so I could not run the suite or the typechecker; `budget-analysis-spreadsheet.ts` carries `// @ts-strict-ignore`, so the type story on the extracted function is reasoned rather than checked; and the one place where the ticket and the code genuinely disagree — Budget Analysis has no per-category grid — means AC-4 and AC-5 as the ticket wrote them are not literally checkable, and I have rewritten them against what the code does. A human reading root_cause should see that correction before the implementer starts.
residual_risks: The 256-character guard on `matches` at sankey-spreadsheet.ts:473 and budget-analysis-spreadsheet.ts:219 is untouched and still disagrees with budgetDataQuery.ts:274-284 in the same direction as before — the ticket puts `matches` out of scope. Pinned in tests[], not fixed.

Sankey and Budget Analysis still apply `customName` conditions that `filterCategoriesByConditions` excludes, and Sankey still returns `false` for an unrecognised `op` where budgetDataQuery.ts returns `true`. Both are pre-existing divergences from the Custom/Grouped reference, outside this ticket, and neither is reachable from the report filter UI.

Neither site has the `isSupportedCategoryCondition` conservative fallback, so a malformed condition (say `contains` with a non-string value) still empties the Budget Analysis axis rather than widening it. Pre-existing, out of scope, and named in out_of_scope.

If QA's browser run cannot reach a report filter whose value is a bare `%` — for instance because the filter input trims or escapes it — AC-1 and AC-4 fall back to the unit cases named in how_to_verify. Both are pinned so neither browser path can fail the ticket on its own.
